9. Complete execution flow

  1. docker compose up --build: DB init → backend upgrades the schema (owner login), creates jal_app, the first accounts and the demo approver, runs retention → ML job writes data and exits → nginx serves the app → backup process starts its loop.
  2. Officers approve the water policy (maker-checker).
  3. Each day: compute and publish the zone timetable; plan tankers for short zones; organisations see their hours.
  4. A requester signs in (consent, optional 2FA) → creates a request (pending).
  5. The admin compares rules (simulate: no writes) → applies one, or overrides with a reason → locked transaction: run (policy, override, comparison), allocations, statuses, water level, notifications, audit → COMMIT.
  6. Sensors update levels and consumption at any time (sharing the reservoir lock).
  7. Decision records and pilot indicators support reviews and audits.

10. OS concepts and implementation

  • Explicit:
    • FCFS, non-preemptive Priority, Round Robin, Water-aware (simulated); manual mode on the same engine;
    • metrics (wait / response, utilisation, Jain, starvation, deadline misses);
    • starvation prevention (per-class floors, deadline pressure, fairness factor);
    • slot scheduling of zones on a shared pump; proportional share with guarantees (water-filling);
    • mutual exclusion: 25 FOR UPDATE, 4 advisory locks, 2 threading.Locks (one in our rate limiter);
    • deadlock prevention by lock order; admission control (rate limit).
  • Indirect: process creation and termination, pipes, exit codes, timeout, threads, system calls, clocks (wall for TOTP, monotonic for limits), process isolation and restart (Docker), file descriptors, buffering, RAII memory handling.
  • Theoretical only: paging, virtual memory, shared memory, real CPU scheduling of our processes.
  • Not implemented: SJF, preemptive priority, EDF, semaphores, message queues.

11. DBMS concepts and implementation

  • 24 tables; PK, 38 FKs (with CASCADE / SET NULL), UNIQUE (composite, expression, 2 partial), 49 CHECKs, NOT NULL, DEFAULT.
  • Mostly 3NF; deliberate JSONB documents and snapshots (policy, timetable, comparison) and two v1.0 exceptions.
  • Transactions (ACID); READ COMMITTED; FOR UPDATE ×25; advisory locks ×4.
  • 49 indexes (17 explicit, 32 automatic).
  • PL/pgSQL triggers (row-level and statement-level); SQL function.
  • JOIN, LATERAL, GROUP BY, HAVING, FILTER, window function ROW_NUMBER, = ANY(array), subqueries, CASE, COALESCE/NULLIF, upsert (DO NOTHING / DO UPDATE), RETURNING, JSONB.
  • DCL: CREATE ROLE, GRANT, REVOKE (least privilege). Backup and restore with pg_dump/pg_restore.
  • Parameterised queries; idempotent migrations; retention.
  • Missing: views, connection pooling, row-level security, point-in-time recovery.

12. Schema and ER model

24 tables. Core: zones 1–N users 1–N water_requests N–1 reservoirs; scheduler_runs M–N water_requests via allocations. ML: consumption (source synthetic/meter/import), predictions, model_evaluations, alerts. Panels: accounts 1–N sessions / notifications / issues / audit_log; schema_info. v2.0: policies (→ runs, timetables), reservoirs 1–N zones (source), supply_timetables 1–N tanker_trips N–1 zones, devices 1–N readings, login_challenges, privacy_requests, security_incidents. See Phase 5 for both diagrams.

13. Important SQL queries

  1. PENDING_SQL (+ FOR UPDATE OF r): the scheduler input.
  2. ZONE_RATIO_SQL: the fairness history.
  3. Relative UPDATE reservoirs SET available_litres = available_litres - %s.
  4. MY_REQUESTS_SQL with LEFT JOIN LATERAL.
  5. The login lookup on lower(email) FOR UPDATE.
  6. The append-only triggers (row and TRUNCATE).
  7. Complaint clusters: GROUP BY … HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3.
  8. Last 7 metered days: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY zone_id ORDER BY recorded_on DESC).
  9. Readings: ON CONFLICT (device_id, measured_at) DO NOTHING; daily totals ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE.
  10. Partial unique indexes for one active policy and one published timetable per day.
  11. GRANT/REVOKE for jal_app.
  12. KPI query with FILTER and = ANY(%s).

14. Main algorithms and business logic

  • Engine: clock after the batch window; pick from the ready list; grant = min(asked, left, cap); refuse if below 20% (not in manual mode); burst = grant ÷ 500; round down to 0.01 L; invariants; metrics.
  • Water-aware score: 0.30·priority + 0.25·urgency + 0.15·scarcity·(1 − share) + 0.15·population + 0.15·(1 − past share), weights from the policy.
  • Cap: max(own share·asked, left − Σ others' share·asked); share from the policy class (0.3 for all in policy v1).
  • Timetable: demand = population × 135 (or metered); target = min(demand, inlet × hours); budget = min(release, pump × hours); floors = zone share × target; rest by water-filling (weight = priority × (1 − share) × target); then earliest continuous slots, most important zone first.
  • Tankers: loads = ⌈(trigger − L/person) × population ÷ tanker size⌉ for zones below the trigger (70 L, 10,000 L in policy v1).
  • Business rules: max 5 pending requests per organisation; request ≤ capacity; sign-ups need approval and consent; 5 wrong passwords → 5-minute lock; sessions 12 h; first admin must change password; policy needs a second officer; override reason ≥ 10 characters; 2FA challenge 5 min / 5 attempts; rate limits 20 and 600 per minute; sensor offline after 30 min; complaint cluster 3 in 48 h.
  • ML: robust z-score (same-weekday median, MAD, K = 3, minimum excess 15%); lag-feature models, 90-day time split, best MAE selected, recursive 7-day forecast; real data per zone from 120 days.

15. Testing strategy and verified results

  • Unit + integration + API tests; hand-calculated scenario; fuzzing; concurrency test; upgrade tests; v2.0 feature tests; browser walkthrough.
  • Verified 18 Oct 2026:
    • C++: 10,425 checks in 33 groups, 0 failures;
    • backend: 77/77 tests (20 in test_v2.py);
    • ML: 11/11 tests;
    • concurrency demo: 80,000 vs 160,000 L.
  • Verified 15 Oct 2026: 12-step browser walkthrough of the v2.0 screens, no CSP violations, no page errors, no sideways scroll at 390 px.
  • Not verified: Docker on Windows, HTTPS profile, backup container and restore, the API as jal_app through real psycopg2, CI on GitHub, DB-down and timeout paths, SQL-injection test, load test.

16. Security considerations

  • PBKDF2-SHA256 (600k iterations, salted), constant-time compare; hashed session tokens (12 h).
  • Lockout; no email enumeration; rate limiting; TOTP two-factor (can be required for admins).
  • RBAC via dependencies; own-organisation filtering (404); maker-checker on policy.
  • Parameterised SQL; no shell; safe dynamic DCL with format(%I, %L).
  • CSP and security headers; HTTPS through Caddy (configured).
  • Least-privilege DB role; audit log protected by two triggers and REVOKE; daily backups (configured).
  • Device keys stored as hashes; DPDP: consent, export, erasure by anonymisation, retention; incident register.
  • Gaps: 2FA secrets unencrypted; secrets in compose/.env; no external audit; HTTPS and backups not yet run; no SSO.

17. Current limitations

  • Synthetic data; demo policy and network values.
  • Organisation allocation: one fixed-rate pipeline, Allocate tab on reservoir 1.
  • Timetable: no hydraulics; greedy, non-preemptive placement; no rotation of hours.
  • Soft deadlines; judgement-based weights (now governed by policy).
  • Water-aware not best on every measure (longest average wait).
  • O(n²) pickers; no connection pool; polling notifications; up to 5 scheduler runs inside a commit's locks.
  • Admin screens English only.
  • Not deployed; not field-tested; not audited.

18. Future improvements

  • P1: laptop run + CI; try HTTPS, backup and restore; confirm jal_app; missing tests.
  • P2: routers, versioned migrations, pool, comparison before locking, parallel scheduler runs, encrypted 2FA secrets.
  • P3: SJF/EDF/preemptive priority, timetable rotation and two windows, explanations, SMS/email, reservoir choice in Allocate.
  • P4 (with a utility): audit, government hosting, SSO, real data, approved policy, shadow-mode pilot, hydraulic checks.

19. Scalability roadmap

  1. Local Compose.
  2. Single server with the HTTPS profile, backups, 2FA required, real secrets (v2.0 has the pieces).
  3. Pilot: pool, workers, monitoring, scheduled jobs, real SCADA gateway.
  4. Production: government hosting, managed DB with replicas and PITR, multiple API instances, CI/CD, SSO.
  5. Distributed: only if measured limits require it.

20. Frequently asked viva questions (shortlist)

  1. Which OS concepts did you implement yourself? → scheduling policies, metrics, starvation prevention (simulated), slot scheduling, plus locking design and one mutex in our code.
  2. How do you prevent double allocation? → the reservoir row lock in one transaction; demo 80k vs 160k.
  3. Isolation level? → READ COMMITTED + FOR UPDATE.
  4. Deadlock? → lock order breaks circular wait; PostgreSQL detects the rest.
  5. Why a child process? → isolation, language independence, timeout.
  6. What is maker-checker? → proposer ≠ approver, enforced in policy.decide() + partial unique index.
  7. How does the timetable work? → floors + water-filling, then earliest continuous pump slots.
  8. How is the audit log protected? → row trigger, TRUNCATE trigger, REVOKE for jal_app.
  9. Paging? SJF? → not implemented; say so.
  10. Ready for a department? → for a pilot setup yes; production needs audit, hosting, SSO and real data.

21. Glossary

TermMeaning
ACIDAtomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability: the transaction guarantees
Advisory lockA PostgreSQL lock on an application-chosen number, used as a cross-process mutex
AgingRaising the priority of long-waiting jobs to stop starvation
APIContract for how programs request things from each other
ASGIStandard interface between Python async web apps and servers (Uvicorn)
B-treeBalanced tree index giving O(log n) lookups
Batch windowMinutes the scheduler waits after the first arrival before deciding ("all" = until the last one)
Bearer tokenA secret sent in the Authorization header proving sign-in
Burst timeTime a job needs the CPU; here litres ÷ 500 L/min
CERT-InIndia's national computer emergency response team; incidents must be reported to it within 6 hours
CHECK constraintA rule each row must satisfy, enforced by the DBMS
Child processA process started by another (parent) process
CIContinuous integration: automatic tests on each change
Coffman conditionsThe four conditions needed for deadlock
CORSBrowser rule controlling calls between different origins (host:port)
CPHEEO norm135 litres per person per day for urban piped supply with sewerage (the default norm in policy v1)
Critical sectionCode that must not run concurrently
CSPContent-Security-Policy: a header limiting where a page may load scripts from and connect to
DCLData Control Language: GRANT and REVOKE
Decision recordPrintable record of an applied plan: rule, policy, who, override reason, litres, alternatives
Dependency injectionA framework supplies a function's needs (DB connection, current user) automatically
Docker image / containerPackaged app / running isolated instance of it
DPDP ActIndia's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023: consent, rights of data principals, breach reporting
Exit codeA number a process returns when it ends (0 = success)
Foreign keyColumn referencing another table's key
Functional dependencyX determines Y
GeoJSONJSON format for map shapes ([longitude, latitude] rings)
GIGWGuidelines for Indian Government Websites (bilingual content, accessibility)
GILCPython lock allowing one thread to run Python bytecode at a time
Guaranteed share (floor)Minimum share reserved for every waiting request or zone (30% in policy v1; per class in v2.0)
HMACA keyed hash; the basis of TOTP codes
HSTSHeader telling browsers to use HTTPS only for this site
IdempotentSafe to run many times with the same result
InvariantA condition that must always hold (e.g. total ≤ available)
IPCInterprocess communication (pipes, sockets, shared memory…)
Jain indexFairness measure (Σx)²/(n·Σx²)
JSONBPostgreSQL binary JSON column type
LATERALSubquery in FROM that can refer to earlier tables in the same FROM
Least privilegeGiving a component only the permissions it needs
lpcdLitres per capita (person) per day
MADMedian absolute deviation: a robust spread measure
MAE / MAPEMean absolute error / mean absolute percentage error
Maker-checkerOne person proposes, a different person approves
MigrationScript that upgrades a database schema
MVCCMulti-version concurrency control: readers see snapshots without blocking writers
MutexLock allowing one holder at a time
Non-preemptiveA running job isn't interrupted
NormalisationStructuring tables to avoid redundancy and anomalies
NUMERIC(12,2)Exact decimal with 2 places
Partial indexIndex over only the rows matching a WHERE condition
PBKDF2Password-hashing function using many iterations
pg_dumpPostgreSQL tool that writes a consistent copy of a database to a file
PipeOne-way byte channel between processes
QuantumRound Robin slice (2,000 L here)
Race conditionBug from timing of concurrent operations
RAIIC++ idiom: objects release resources in their destructors
Rate limitingRefusing a client's requests above N per time window
RBACRole-based access control
READ COMMITTEDIsolation level: each statement sees committed data
Reverse proxyServer that receives requests and forwards them to servers behind it (Caddy)
Robust z-scoreOutlier score using the median and MAD instead of the mean and SD
Row lock (FOR UPDATE)Exclusive lock on selected rows until commit
SaltRandom value added before hashing so equal passwords differ
SCADASupervisory control and data acquisition: systems that collect field readings
Shadow modeRecording the system's recommendation without acting on it (pilot evidence)
StarvationA job never gets the resource
Synthetic dataData generated by our code, not measured
System callRequest from a program to the OS kernel
TOTPTime-based one-time password (RFC 6238)
TransactionAll-or-nothing group of DB operations
TriggerDB code run automatically on table events (per row or per statement)
WALWrite-ahead log: PostgreSQL's durability mechanism
Water-fillingProportional sharing that caps full consumers and re-shares their surplus
Window functionSQL function computed over a partition of rows without collapsing them

Final wrap-up

You now have the complete map of v2.0: what the project does, how each technology and important piece of code works, which OS and DBMS concepts are genuinely implemented (and which are not), what v2.0 added for a water department, what has been verified, where it's weak, and how to improve and defend it.
